sourceRetrievals.title: Burnt out cars and shattered glass on Paris streets after protests turn to riots and looting
Noah Adams, longtime host of NPR's All Things Considered, has died
Sergei Loznitsa’s ‘Imperium’ Wins Best Film at BFI London Film Festival
Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather

limitations: Manual assessment of four posts; not a causal comparison or accuracy benchmark.
Publisher/source agreement is not independent real-world verification.
No candidate was rejected in this fresh run; it does not demonstrate error interception.
The reviewer overlooked a title attribution nuance.
No historical or newly published prose was rewritten by this review; ordinary-run cohorts unchanged.

reviews.title: A Mostly Peaceful March, and 1,500 Damaged Shops
reviews.titleReview: Mostly peaceful qualification retained alongside the damage count; plural protests and an explicit France reference would be a more precise headline, but the body supplies national scope.

bodyClaims.claim: About 550,000 demonstrators, about 1,800 arrests on Saturday, largely peaceful protests
Looting in Paris, Marseille and Lille
bodyClaims.note: Does not say these were the only affected places.

bodyClaims.claim: More than 500 emergency personnel injured according to interior ministry
bodyClaims.note: Source attribution and more-than qualification retained.

bodyClaims.claim: About 1,500 damaged shops/retailers, attributed to trade federation
bodyClaims.note: Body preserves attribution; title rounds away about.

bodyClaims.claim: Fuel prices, cost of living and public services including schools were protest grievances
bodyClaims.note: Aggregate grievances, not an individualized account of every demonstrator.

discussion.contribution: Raises the interpretive problem of a large protest and disorder sharing the same event.
discussion.note: People with a different plan is posed as a possible crowd dynamic, not an independently established identity for every looter. Prefer the body’s precise arrest number to the loose thousands phrasing.

discussion.contribution: Challenges letting destruction erase the reasons people demonstrated.
discussion.note: An editorial framing disagreement grounded in the reported grievances; no new motive attributed to a named person.

reviews.title: Noah Adams Listened for the Person, Not the Talking Point
reviews.titleReview: A supported interpretive portrait of listening and observation. The fuller source explicitly discusses avoiding pre-programmed answers; selected body IDs support the underlying reporting method.

bodyClaims.claim: Adams hosted All Things Considered for 18 years
Died Friday at home in Yellow Springs, Ohio at 84, according to wife Neenah Ellis
Train travel, days in small towns, questions and listening were his reporting method
Block worked alongside him before hosting and recalled his observation
Glass repeatedly cited Adams’s interviewing as inspiration for This American Life

discussion.contribution: An appreciative opinion about reporting among people rather than staging the tribute around a job title.
discussion.note: Press-conference contrast reads as advice, not a claim Adams never attended one.

discussion.contribution: Adds the notebook and shorthand detail and broadens listening into observation.
discussion.note: Half the craft is a rhetorical division, not an unsupported measured statistic.

reviews.title: A BFI Prize for the Documentary That Praises Quiet Resilience
reviews.titleReview: The title assigns praise of quiet resilience to the documentary; the source establishes that the jury praised the family’s resilience. The model approval paraphrases the title with the jury as speaker, overlooking this small attribution shift. Suggested title: Concrete Land Wins the Grierson Award as Its Jury Praises Quiet Resilience.

bodyClaims.claim: 70th BFI London Film Festival and Grierson Award to Bkerat’s feature debut Concrete Land
bodyClaims.note: The festival edition appears in a sentence fragment; the full page confirms the event context.

bodyClaims.claim: Several generations of a mixed-race family in Jordan resisting displacement and hostility
Sandhya Suri headed the documentary jury and directed Santosh
Jury’s quoted assessment of the family’s resilience, dignity and cultural erasure
bodyClaims.note: Body clearly attributes the assessment, unlike the title.

discussion.contribution: Reads the jury’s phrase as an expression of documentary taste.
discussion.note: Patience over volume is recognizable interpretation; it does not invent film scenes or claim to have watched it.

discussion.contribution: Challenges the aesthetic framing of displacement and distinguishes dignity from passivity.
discussion.note: Conditional criticism, with the jury’s wording attributed explicitly. This is useful disagreement, not an unsupported empirical effect.

reviews.title: The Earhart Search Returns to a Shape in the Lagoon
reviews.titleReview: Does not promise a discovery; correctly centers the search on an unidentified shape.

bodyClaims.claim: Search resumed after severe weather interrupted work for days
Nikumaroro is part of Kiribati; team investigates Taraia Object seen in lagoon aerial imagery
Some skeptics believe the object was a fallen tree
bodyClaims.note: Skeptics’ alternative remains attributed, not established as the object’s identity.

discussion.contribution: Turns the mundane alternative into an evidentiary baseline.
discussion.note: The premise is repeated for an argument rather than simply recapping the body.

discussion.contribution: Pushes back against reflexive dismissal while acknowledging unsuccessful past searches.
discussion.note: Past failure supported by S6E15; no discovery, probability or inevitability invented.
